Chapter 7: The Toll of Activism—Burnout, Loss, and the Need for Healing.
Carrying the weight of a movement…it comes with a price, doesn’t it? For so many people, activism becomes all-consuming.
Days start to blur into nights, and suddenly, there’s barely a line between your own life and the struggles you’re fighting for. With every headline—one more shooting, one more injustice—it gets harder to catch your breath, let alone rest.
Imagine an organizer who’s always the first to show up and the last to leave. At first, she’s fueled by hope and determination. But over time, cracks begin to show. Sleep slips away. That spark, once so bright, is dimmed by exhaustion and doubt.
Friends see the shift. They urge her to slow down, to take care of herself. But when the movement feels so urgent, how do you step away? It almost feels impossible.
And then there’s loss. Grief is woven into the very fabric of the movement. Every new tragedy reopens wounds that never really heal. Funerals and memorials become part of everyday life—spaces where sorrow and solidarity are always side by side.
There’s so much pressure to be strong, to keep pushing forward no matter what. But over time, the truth becomes unavoidable: nobody can carry this burden alone.
Healing—a word that might’ve once felt like a luxury—turns out to be a necessity. Organizers start carving out spaces for rest and reflection. They open up about their struggles and lean on each other for support. Therapy, meditation, even little acts of self-care—they become tools for survival.
The movement learns something vital: taking care of each other is just as important as any protest, any petition. A meal shared after a grueling day. A simple check-in call. A burst of laughter in the chaos. It’s these small acts of kindness that hold everything together.
So, it becomes clear—the fight for justice isn’t only about changing the world. It’s also about changing how we treat ourselves and each other. Healing isn’t separate from the work… it’s at the very heart of it.
And when organizers care for themselves, they find the strength to keep going, to keep believing, and to keep dreaming of a better world.
